title: Dev/Prod Parity: Mock APIs vs. Netlify Redirects — Check

questions.prompt: In `netlify.toml`, what does a redirect with `status = 200` do?
questions.explanation: A status 200 redirect is a rewrite: the public URL is preserved while Netlify internally routes to the function, passing the remaining path via `:splat`.
options: Issues a 301 permanent redirect that changes the browser URL
Rewrites the request internally so the browser URL stays the same while a function serves it
Blocks the request and returns an empty 200 response

questions.prompt: Why should the local mock route on the same path semantics that production uses (parsing the splat)?
questions.explanation: If the mock decides routing differently than production, your local tests exercise a different code path and parity breaks down.
options: To make the mock run faster
So the mock faithfully reflects how production selects a domain module, avoiding green-local/broken-prod surprises
To reduce the number of domain modules

questions.prompt: A faithful local mock should only ever return clean, successful responses so tests stay simple.
questions.explanation: Production sees timeouts, partial failures, and malformed responses. A mock that can reproduce those failure modes lets you test the frontend's error handling before users hit it.
